messages:
support_jordan: Customer reports gaps in SIEM after yesterday's retention policy update — about ~2h of events missing for tenant `acme-corp`. They say export job completed and S3 shows objects, but the SIEM index has holes. Can eng-security take a look?

alice_support: thanks for flagging — do we have the export job id + manifest? also which KMS key did they use during the window?

support_jordan: job id 89421, manifest at s3://redwood-exports/acme/89421/manifest.json, KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd-rotation-2026 — customer says they rotated keys on 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC (before job).

nick_eng_sre: first pass: if objects exist but SIEM is missing fields maybe some batches were partially consumed or stripped by the forwarder. Any evidence of decryption errors in forwarder logs?

carla_security: I scanned the forwarder logs for 89421. No obvious KMS AccessDenied. But I see repeated "batch: partial_upload" entries and a couple of "skipping tenant filter" log lines around 02:12 UTC. Snippet: ```2026-03-04T02:12:18Z audit-forwarder[pid=42]: WARN partial_upload batch_id=0x7a3 tenant=acme-corp size_bytes=0 -> retrying```

support_jordan: customer also attached SIEM raw ingestion lines; they show events with missing identity fields (user_id null) for a contiguous range.

nick_eng_sre: hmm. Could be two distinct issues: 1) prefix filter logic accidentally dropped some events during the retention backfill, 2) replay tool truncated or replayed wrong timebuckets. Let's reproduce locally for that tenant and time window.

replay-tool-bot: Replay job started: replay-20260304-89421-acme (params: --start 2026-03-04T01:50Z --end 2026-03-04T04:00Z)

nick_eng_sre: repro steps I ran: `./tools/replay --tenant acme-corp --start 2026-03-04T02:00Z --end 2026-03-04T03:30Z --job 89421` -> saw same partial batches and the replayer logged "trimmed trailing null fields" for some protobuf messages.

carla_security: that trimmed message looks like an older serializer edge-case. Could be related to the new retention compactor that collapses tombstones; compactor may emit a slightly different schema for deleted events and our forwarder filter misinterprets it.

alice_support: customer demands root cause and whether PII got dropped. Also asks if replays will preserve ordering/ids.

nick_eng_sre: action plan: (A) collect one affected object from S3 and run `audit-inspect` to decode raw payload and show fields (need example event id from customer) (B) run forwarder in debug mode on a replica and capture decryption + transform logs (C) if schema mismatch, produce a one-off migration to normalize deleted-event records before forwarding.

support_jordan: customer provided sample object key: `s3://redwood-exports/acme/89421/part-0003.gz` and event id `evt_20260304_1273`.

carla_security: I pulled the object and decoded. The payload contains records where `identity` is `{\"type\":\"delete\"}` instead of the usual object with `user_id`. The forwarder transform expects `identity.user_id` for enrichment and if absent it drops the field. That explains missing identity in SIEM, but not why these records were included in the export at all.

nick_eng_sre: that points to compactor producing compacted tombstones in place of full events during the retention window. We need timeline: retention run @ 02:05Z, compactor v2.1 deployed on 2026-03-03, key rotation at 02:00Z on 03-04. Could be coincidence.

security-ops: agreed — high priority. Risk: SIEM missing identity may affect SOC alerts. Notify SOC and legal.

replay-tool-bot: Replay job completed: replay-20260304-89421-acme — status=partial_failures(3)

carla_security: repro confirms 3 partial failures where records were converted to tombstones. Temporary mitigation: re-run export with `--include-deletes false` flag to skip tombstone-only batches (so SIEM gets only full events). Also we can run a one-off normalizer `./tools/normalize --input s3://redwood-exports/acme/89421/part-0003.gz --output s3://redwood-exports/acme/89421/normalized/` which will expand tombstones to a placeholder identity to keep SIEM happy.

alice_support: propose telling customer: 1) root cause: compactor emitted tombstone-only records during retention backfill, forwarder treated them as missing identity; 2) remit: we can re-run export with normalize or re-send normalized batches; 3) we will backfill SIEM with normalized artifacts and provide timeline. Any objections? :eyes:

nick_eng_sre: +1. Also add internal fix: make forwarder tolerant of tombstone identity schema and add a unit test for compactor-forwarder contract.

support_jordan: I'll send the support note and schedule a re-export window with customer for 2026-03-05 02:00-03:00 UTC. Customer asked for a post-mortem.

carla_security: created incident ticket INC-2026-3125 and assigned to eng-security for root cause + remediation steps. I included logs and normalized sample in the ticket.

security-ops: also rotate delegated replay key to ensure no drift.

support_jordan: thanks team. I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and ETA. :thumbsup:

nick_eng_sre: follow-ups: (1) PR to forwarder to accept tombstone identity (small), (2) compactor to tag tombstone-only batches with header `x-audit-tombstone: true`, (3) automated regression test for replay. I'll take (1) and (3).

carla_security: I'll own compactor tagging change and coordinate release schedule.

support_jordan: closing here once re-export completes and customer confirms SIEM catch-up.
